addedLines: - chiron: Chiron (hera-triage) — post-session self-improvement agent for the HERA stack. Archives the session, builds the triage queue from all note streams, drafts dispositions and diffs, walks the human through rulings, lands the amendments, and keeps the corpus from growing monotonically. (Tools: All tools)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- hera-session: HERA session-init — the front door for a measurement session. Interviews rig / device / brief / autonomy, builds the session dir with hera-mksession, fills the notebook's device slots from the device card, preflights JupyterLab, and hands off to hera-tactical. (Tools: All tools)

- hera-tactical: HERA tactical — drives measurement sessions with a human operator at the controls. Protocol only; machine facts come from the deployed rig card. Campaign scope set by the session brief. Reads rig card, device card, and live notebook; lands runnable cells via nb-collab. (Tools: All tools)

- iris: IRIS — chat-first collaborator for live toploader measurement sessions. Boots from prior state, follows the operator's lead, types cells when asked. Same tool surface as HERA tactical but inverted social contract — the human drives, IRIS supports. (Tools: All tools)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- nb: nb — Jupyter notebook navigator
- nb-collab: nb-collab — append cells to a live JupyterLab notebook
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

=== toploader rig card: Identity ===
# Rig card — toploader

*Rig-level machine facts for the Sharpe Lab toploader cryostat.
Canonical copy: `hera/rig-cards/toploader.md` in the `measurement-env`
repo; deployed as `rig_card.md` next to `device_card.md` in the
measurement directory. Errors or gaps found in-session go to
`session_notes.md`, not this file — agents are read-only on the repo.*

## Identity
- **Rig**: toploader — dilution-refrigerator cryostat with a
  top-loading probe; sample base ≈ **30 mK** (probe MC). Which insert is
  loaded is per-cooldown → device card.
- **Rig owner**: Aaron
- **Control PC**: `toploader` (Windows 11); measurement dirs under
  `~/measurements/<user>/<session>/`
- **Bring-up**: the launcher GUI (`uv run measurement-env` in
  `~/measurement_env`) owns run creation (dated templates), JupyterLab
  (rooted at `~/measurements`), the hardware workers, and the
  aggregate health panel
- **Status**: in service

## Magnet

- **Controller**: AMI Model 430 (qcodes `AMIModel430`),
  `TCPIP0::192.168.0.101::7180::SOCKET`. Out-of-plane field, Tesla,
  via `magnet.field()`.
- **Coil constant**: 0.116783 T/A (`sharpelab_nb.constants.TOPLOADER`).
- **Absolute field ceiling**: **±9 T** — AMI430 hardware limit
  (Isaac, 2026-06-18); the driver raises if `|target| > COIL? ×
  current_limit`. The session cap (device card / SAFETIES) is what
  measurements obey.
- **Read-truth**: `magnet.field()` returns the **measured** readback;
  the set-point is not readable as field — never infer field from the
  last set call.
- **Set semantics**: `magnet.field(target)` **blocks** until the supply
  reports holding (busy-polls `ramping_state`).
- **Interrupt ≠ stop**: the ramp is commanded before the blocking poll,
  so a kernel interrupt during the wait leaves the supply ramping to its
  last target — recovery is calling `magnet.field()` again.
- **Ramp rate**: instrument-configured, not a code constant — read the

*Per-device card for the zf1 dual-device chip on the **toploader** rig.
Deployed into the measurement directory; mutates per cooldown.*

## Identity
- **Device id**: `zf1`
- **Material**: Bernal bilayer graphene + WSe₂ (Aaron, 2026-06-06;
  bilayer above WSe₂)
- **Owner**: isaac (`izheng`)
- **Fridge**: toploader. Sample base ≈ 30 mK, electron T ≈ 40 mK
  (rotator probe loaded)
- **Dual-device chip**: top + bottom halves, separately gated. Bottom
  half is wired and used; top half is not.
- **Status**: cold; single cooldown (inserted 2026-04-15)

## Gate stack (geometry prior)
- **Dual graphite gates** (top + back), **no SiO₂** (Aaron, 2026-06-06).
- `t_tg` ≈ **23.6 nm**, `t_bg` = **20 nm** (cap ratio **1.18**);
  `κ_hBN` = 3.

content.content:
=== notebook policy ===
{'policy': 'append_only'}

=== slot cells (id / slot / source) ===

----- slot=gate-validators  id=c16  type=code -----
# slot: gate-validators — operating limits from the device card's gate-
# operating-limits table; commit EXACTLY the card numbers. Each value
# `# <-- validate`.
TG_MIN, TG_MAX = -7.0, +6.0   # top gate (k_tg), V    # <-- validate
BG_MIN, BG_MAX = -4.0, +4.2   # back gate (k_bg), V    # <-- validate
k_tg.volt.vals = validators.Numbers(TG_MIN, TG_MAX)
k_bg.volt.vals = validators.Numbers(BG_MIN, BG_MAX)

# Limit lists for sanitize_tg_bg()
tg_lims, bg_lims = [TG_MIN, TG_MAX], [BG_MIN, BG_MAX]

# Session field cap — machine-enforced: magnet.field is a qcodes Parameter, so
# this validator rejects magnet.field(target) with |B| > cap before any
# hardware traffic. Driver backstop: |B| <= COIL? x current_limit (~9 T) on the
# AMI430 unit.
B_SESSION_CAP = 5.0  # Tesla    # <-- validate (session cap from card/brief)
magnet.field.vals = validators.Numbers(-B_SESSION_CAP, B_SESSION_CAP)

# Sample-heater ceiling for sustained runs (V, not T — open-loop drive).
HEATER_V_MAX = 6.5  # V    # <-- validate
heater.volt.vals = validators.Numbers(0, HEATER_V_MAX)

# DC current-bias range (SRS DC205 hardware: +/-15 V -> +/-150 nA at 100 MOhm).
dc205_1.volt.vals = validators.Numbers(-15, 15)

----- slot=geometry  id=c19  type=code -----
# slot: geometry — gate-stack thicknesses from the device card's Gate-stack
# geometry (geometry prior — calibrate cnp-and-dline-calibration before
# trusting derived scales). Each value `# <-- validate`.
t_tg = 23.6e-9   # top-gate hBN thickness, m    # <-- validate
t_bg = 20e-9     # back-gate hBN thickness, m    # <-- validate
t_bgSiO2 = 0     # SiO2 term, m — zero for a metal/graphite back gate    # <-- validate

# Session gate calibration. cal.n_D(V_tg, V_bg) -> (n [m^-2], D [V/m]);
# set n_offset / D_offset from cnp-and-dline-calibration once live.
cal = GateCalibration.from_thicknesses(t_tg, t_bg, t_bgSiO2)

----- slot=meas-config  id=c21  type=code -----
# slot: meas-config — channel/contact assignments + gains from the device
# card's Measurement setup (current channel + gain, provided contact
# configuration). Each value `# <-- validate`. Toploader contacts are wired
# DIRECT (no QSwitch) — name the contact pair per channel. Always set 'comment'
# per run — structured, current, no inherited text.
meas_config = {
